title: Elastic cross-cluster API key in the local cluster keystore
summary: The encoded value of a cross-cluster API key added to the local cluster's keystore, the only place Elastic documents the key being used.
rationale: Claim cross-cluster-key-carrier-is-local-cluster-keystore records that the encoded value is added to the local cluster's keystore and provided on each request to the remote cluster, and claim cross-cluster-key-refused-on-rest-interface records that it is not an Authorization header value. The snippets read do not name the keystore setting (open question cross-cluster-keystore-setting-name-not-recorded), so no keystore slot can be written as a carrier without guessing. The type is not visible in the encoded string (cross-cluster-no-independent-lexical-signal), and its alphabet and padding are not stated (cross-cluster-encoded-alphabet-padding). The create-response members are covered by a separate Case. Contract claims cited: cross-cluster-api-key/cross-cluster-key-carrier-is-local-cluster-keystore, cross-cluster-api-key/cross-cluster-key-refused-on-rest-interface.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled by: the Elastic remote cluster setup page that names the keystore setting, recorded as a source.

sources.supports: Copy the encoded key (`encoded` in the response) to a safe location. It is required for the local cluster configuration.
To enable this, add the API key to the local cluster's keystore.
The local cluster is configured to provide this API key on each request to the remote cluster.
A `cross_cluster` API key cannot be used to authenticate through the REST interface.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
